title: Protocol for differential centrifugation-based separation and characterization of apoptotic vesicles derived from human mesenchymal stem cells
protocol: Put the apoptosis-inducing solution and PBS into a 37°C water bath for pre-heating.
Aspirate the complete culture medium.
Add 5 mL pre-warmed PBS to rinse the cells for 10 s, and then aspirate the PBS.
Repeat step of rinsing with PBS once.
Add 5 mL pre-warmed apoptosis-inducing solution to each dish.
Incubate the cells in a humidified 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 12 h.
Flush the cells thoroughly with pipetting the conditioned media to detach all apoptotic cells when approximately 90% of the cells undergo apoptosis.
Transfer the supernatant, together with detached cells, to a sterile 15 mL centrifuge tube on ice.
Rinse each dish with 2 mL cold PBS, and transfer the PBS to the same centrifuge tube.
Place the centrifuge tubes in a centrifuge.
Centrifuge the samples for 10 min at 800 × g at 4°C to remove cells and cell debris.
Place the centrifuge rotor in the centrifuge machine.
Position 1.5 mL EP tubes symmetrically within the rotor.
Centrifuge the tubes at 16,000 × g for 30 min at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant with a pipette and discard the cell debris.
Divide the collected supernatant into five 1.5 mL EP tubes.
Place the EP tubes in a centrifuge symmetrically.
Centrifuge the tubes at 16,000 × g for 30 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from each tube carefully.
Add 200 μL cold PBS to each tube and gently resuspend the pellet by pipetting.
Merge the suspension of every five EP tubes into one EP tube.
Centrifuge the merged sample tubes at 16,000 × g for 30 min at 4°C.
Tilt EP tubes to make supernatant parallel to precipitation.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add 1 mL cold PBS to each tube and gently resuspend the pellet by pipetting.
Centrifuge the tubes at 16,000 × g for 30 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Re-suspend the precipitate with 50 μL cold PBS and store at 4°C for nanoparticle tracking analysis.
Re-suspend the precipitate with 50 μL cold PBS and store at 4°C for TEM analysis.
Re-suspend the precipitates from two dishes with 50 μL lysis buffer.
Incubate on ice for 30 min.
Store at −80°C for Western blotting analysis.
Take 10 μL of the sample and dilute to 10 mL with PBS.
Inject at least 5 mL ddH2O into the ZetaView® BASIC NTA machine channel at a constant speed (0.5 mL/s to 1 mL/s) until the number of particles displayed on the detection interface is less than 10.
Prepare calibration solution by diluting 1 μL provided with the NTA machine to 1 mL with ddH2O, then taking 100 μL and diluting to 25 mL with ddH2O.
Inject at least 5 mL of calibration solution into the machine channel until the number of particles displayed on the detection interface is between 50-400 (preferably around 200).
Run the calibration program when particle count is appropriate.
Clean the machine channel by repeating step 16.
Use a sterile 10 mL syringe to inject at least 5 mL buffer solution (PBS) at a constant speed of 0.5 mL/s to 1 mL/s.
Tap the side of the syringe gently while holding it upright to drain any bubbles in the sample before injection.
Inject at least 2 mL of the sample into the machine channel using a sterile 1 mL syringe.
Hold the syringe upright and tap the side gently to remove bubbles from the sample before injecting.
If the particle count on the detection interface is too high, repeat step 16 immediately to avoid particles retention at the channel wall.
Use PBS to dilute the sample further until the number of particles displayed on the detection interface is less than 10.
Conduct particle capture analysis and generate an analysis report.
Clean the sample in the channel by repeating step 21 if contaminants are found or troubleshooting is required.
Clean the PBS in the channel by repeating step 16.
Use a sterile 10 mL syringe to inject at least 10 mL of air at a constant speed of 0.5 mL/s to 1 mL/s to remove ddH2O from the channel.
Drop 10 μL of the sample onto a copper mesh for TEM analysis.
Incubate the droplet on the copper mesh for 10 min at 25°C.
Remove excess liquid with filter paper.
Mix the suspension well before pipetting from the middle of the liquid.
Pipette and drop the diluted sample to the front side of the copper mesh for clear observation under TEM.
Rinse the copper mesh in 100 μL sterile ddH2O and remove excess liquid with filter paper.
Repeat rinsing of the copper mesh in 100 μL sterile ddH2O two more times.
Immerse the front side of the copper mesh in 2% uranyl acetate solution for 1 min at 25°C.
Remove excess liquid with filter paper after negatively staining the copper mesh.
Repeat step to remove excess liquid with filter paper and place the copper mesh on a new filter paper.
Dry the copper mesh under an incandescent lamp for 2 min or at room temperature (25°C) for 10 min.
Observe the copper mesh under a TEM operating at 100 kV.
Centrifuge the lysates at 13,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a sterile 1.5 mL EP tube.
Prepare 0.5 mg/mL BSA standard solution.
Dilute 0.5 mg/mL BSA standard solution with normal saline to a serial concentration.
Add 20 μL of standard solution at different concentrations into each standard well of the 96-well plate.
Add 2 μL sample and 18 μL normal saline into each sample well of the 96-well plate.
Mix BCA reagent A and BCA reagent B in a 50 : 1 ratio to make the needed amount of working solution.
Add 200 μL working solution to each well.
Incubate the 96-well plate in an incubator at 37°C for 30 min.
Measure the optical density (OD) value at the wavelength of 562 nm using a microplate reader.
Establish the standard curve according to the OD data and calculate the protein concentration of each sample.
Dilute the samples to 1 μg/μL with normal saline and 5 × loading buffer.
Seal the tubes with parafilm.
Heat the sealed tubes at 95°C for 5 min.
Load equal protein mass per sample onto a precast 4%–20% (wt/vol) TGX stain-free gel.
Run the SDS-PAGE at 80 V for the concentrated gel and 120 V for the separation gel.
Transfer the gel to a PVDF membrane using a wet transfer system for 120 min at 200 mA.
Rinse the PVDF membrane in methanol for 20 s immediately before transferring.
Block the membrane in 1 × TBST containing 5% BSA for 2 h at 25°C with gentle shaking.
Incubate the membrane with primary antibodies diluted in 1 × TBST at 4°C for 12–16 h with gentle shaking.
Wash the membrane in 1 × TBST for 10 min at 25°C on a shaker.
Repeat the washing step two more times.
Incubate the membrane with secondary antibodies diluted in 1 × TBST for 1 h at 25°C on a shaker.
Wash the membrane in 1 × TBST for 10 min at 25°C on a shaker.
Repeat washing the membrane with 1 × TBST for 10 min at 25°C on a shaker.
Incubate the membrane with the reagents of an ECL kit for 1 min away from light.
Detect the protein bands by a gel imaging system.
